title: Society and culture
description: Words for family, generations, traditions, globalisation, equality and community life.

words.definition: the process by which businesses, cultures and economies become connected around the world
words.example: Globalisation has made foreign food and films part of everyday life.

words.definition: traditions, buildings and culture passed down from earlier generations
words.example: Batik was recognised by UNESCO as part of Indonesia's cultural heritage.

words.definition: differences in attitudes and values between older and younger people
words.example: Technology has widened the generation gap in many families.

words.definition: an unfair difference between groups in wealth, rights or opportunities
words.example: Income inequality has grown in many countries despite economic growth.

words.definition: to become part of a new society and adopt its customs
words.example: Learning the local language helps immigrants assimilate into their new community.

words.definition: the presence of many different types of people or things
words.example: Indonesia's ethnic diversity is reflected in its hundreds of regional languages.

words.definition: a fixed, oversimplified idea about a type of person or group
words.example: Films often reinforce negative stereotypes about certain nationalities.

words.definition: a behaviour that is considered normal and acceptable in a society
words.example: In some cultures, it is a social norm for adult children to live with their parents.

words.definition: a family including grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins
words.example: Many Indonesian children are raised with the help of their extended family.

words.definition: a family of two parents and their children only
words.example: Urbanisation has made the nuclear family more common than the extended family.

words.definition: treated as unimportant and excluded from power or society
words.example: Public libraries provide vital services for marginalised communities.

words.definition: to offer to do work without being paid
words.example: Students who volunteer in their community often develop greater empathy.

words.definition: behaving in the same way as most other people
words.example: Strict school uniforms are sometimes criticised for encouraging conformity.

words.definition: caring too much about money and possessions
words.example: Advertising is often blamed for making young people more materialistic.

words.definition: an accepted, traditional way of behaving in a society
words.example: It is a local custom to take off your shoes before entering someone's home.

words.definition: the feeling of belonging to a group with a shared culture
words.example: Speaking a regional language helps young people maintain their cultural identity.

words.definition: consisting of parts or people that are all the same or similar
words.example: Critics fear that globalisation will create a homogeneous world culture.

words.definition: giving money or help to people in need
words.example: Philanthropy by wealthy individuals funds many hospitals and universities.

words.definition: with members who support and care about each other
words.example: Villages tend to have more close-knit communities than big cities.

words.definition: a person of the same age or status as you
words.example: Teenagers often care more about the opinions of their peers than their parents.

words.definition: a person who others admire and copy
words.example: Sports stars have a responsibility to act as positive role models.

words.definition: treating people unfairly because of their race, gender, age or other characteristics
words.example: Laws against discrimination in hiring have helped more women enter senior roles.

words.definition: differences in income, services and lifestyle between cities and the countryside
words.example: Better roads and internet could narrow the urban-rural divide.

words.definition: belonging to the original people or species of a place
words.example: Indigenous communities often have deep knowledge of local plants and medicine.

words.definition: the degree to which people in a society feel connected and work together
words.example: Shared public spaces such as parks can strengthen social cohesion.

words.definition: the way a child is raised and taught by parents
words.example: A strict upbringing does not always produce well-behaved adults.

words.definition: great public interest in the lives of famous people
words.example: Celebrity culture can give young people unrealistic expectations about success.

words.definition: willingness to accept beliefs and behaviour different from your own
words.example: Schools play a key role in teaching religious tolerance.

words.definition: to gradually weaken or destroy something
words.example: Some argue that social media is eroding traditional family values.

words.definition: to encourage something to develop
words.example: Community festivals foster a sense of belonging among residents.
